newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Calment, world's oldest person, turns 122.
newsitem.headline: France's Calment, world's oldest person, turns 122.

text.p: France's Jeanne Calment, officially the oldest woman in the world and famed for her wit, celebrates a subdued 122nd birthday on Friday in a life that began in an era before films, telephones, cars or aircraft.

Blind, confined to a wheelchair and all but deaf, the white-haired Calment will spend her birthday at the Maison du Lac retirement home in Arles, the southern French town where she has always lived and once met Vincent van Gogh as a girl.
Anxious to protect the increasingly frail "Doyenne of Humanity" from exploitation as she sets new longevity records with every heartbeat, doctors are to scale back the partying of recent years.

A court in January ordered her to be placed under legal guardianship, ruling she was no longer able to carry out basic civic acts and "she needs to be counselled, supported and protected from the upsets that her fame can cause."
On her 121st birthday, for instance, a music company issued a compact disc entitled "Mistress of Time" that featured Calment talking to a background of funk-rap, techno and dance music.
The pop star aura seemed a jolt for Calment, whose favourite music includes Bizet's opera Carmen, first performed in 1875, the year of her birth.
And for her 121st birthday, there was a huge party with Camargue horses, children in local costume, confectionery and garlands of flowers in Arles.

The Guinness Book of Records lists Calment as the oldest person who ever lived -- and has a birth certificate, dated February 21, 1875, to prove the claim. It says other rivals for the longevity crown lack documentation.

They include a former Brazilian slave, Maria do Carmen Geronimo, who celebrated a 125th birthday last March. And newspapers from the United Arab Emirates said in July 1996 that a man, Ali Matar bin Ghourair, had just died aged 136.
Calment's cheerful sense of humour has won her fame as much as her longevity. A long-time smoker who enjoys a glass of port, Calment has said a smile is her recipe for long life.
"I've only ever had one wrinkle and I'm sitting on it," she once remarked. On another, she predicted: "I will die laughing."
Born 10 years after the assassination of U.S. president Abraham Lincoln and four years before scientist Albert Einstein, she always lived in the southern France town of Arles and never worked.

Van Gogh, who immortalised southern France in his paintings, may have bought canvasses from her father's shop when she was a girl. She has described him as "ugly as sin...bad tempered, a grumbler and smelling of alcohol".

She married in 1896 and her husband, Fernand Calment, died in 1942 -- four years before their golden wedding anniversary. "Queen Jeanne" outlived all her descendants. Her daughter died in 1934 and her grandson, a doctor, in 1963.
